reviews.title: From the Gym to My Living Room — Total Game Changer
reviews.text:
I was first introduced to LES MILLS at the gym, and from my very first class, I could feel the challenge. I decided to embrace it, stay consistent, and the results truly transformed my body and the way I trained.

Now, being able to bring those same intense, effective workouts into my own home is a total game changer. The workouts push you, give you that satisfying burn, and make you feel like you’re actually training with purpose. I love that I can get the LES MILLS experience whenever I want, right from my living room. If you want workouts that challenge you and help you feel stronger and fitter, this is it.

reviews.title: Not compatible with device
reviews.text: While I love the workouts Les Mills provides, it’s all pointless as they don’t allow access through TV apps. Doing any class from several feet away while looking at my phone screen is impossible. And casting from my phone to my TV is a severe lag, so instruction and demonstration never match up. It also drains my phone battery significantly. Horrible user experience - there is little thought into the digital aspects of connection to the obvious physical application of content. Stinks I’m paying a subscription for an app I can’t use for however many months until they launch a TV compatible application.

reviews.title: Still not a great replacement for the old iOS app
reviews.text:
I switched over from the old Apple TV app and there are so many things I can’t do any more

1. I can’t browse the entire collection of Body ______ apps. It only shows the last 10. So if I want to do Body Combat 86, I have to search for it or favorite it. 

2. You can’t add favorites via this app.

3. No release notes. I used to look through Body Pump release notes to see if they had an emphasis on push-ups or a certain move. Can’t do that any more.

4. Still no filter for English v Spanish? I accidentally click the wrong one sometimes and it’s super annoying.

5. The activity counter (“active this month” and “average duration” is useless and demotivating if you only use the Apple TV app. Because it doesn’t increment.

6. Non-native iOS keyboard means my mom can’t use dictation and has to type to find the release she’s looking for. Not ideal.

 7. Why are we still auto playing? I just finished a workout. This isn’t a Netflix series. I’m not going for an immediate round 2.

Right now, I’m switching back and forth between the old app and the new just for the release notes. Sometimes I don’t want to go by favorites. I just want to browse.

Last I logged onto the website, there were filters for instructors too. It’s be nice to have more of that functionality in the TV app. I don’t pre-select workouts online or on the mobile app. I browse through when I’m about to workout and I don’t have any intention to change that behavior.

Bottom line is that I only use the Les Mills TV app, and I know I’m not alone. This new app I’m being forced to use on Apple TV just isn’t there for me yet.

reviews.title: Walking Workouts
reviews.text: The most exceptional, and by far the best fitness app that I’ve ever seen. I would like to see walking workouts. As we get older, not all of our bodies can respond to HIIT workouts or anything that is high impact. It would be great for those of us aging fitness enthusiast to do 4000 and 5000 step count walking workouts (30 minutes, 45 minutes, and 1 hour workouts). Keep up the good work. No one can hold a candle to Les Mills+.
